requirements.verifier_assertion: test_merge_lock_command_is_available: `pdm merge-lock --help` returns 0 and stdout contains the token `--on-conflict`.

test_clean_three_way_merge: alpha bumped to 1.1.0 (ours) and beta bumped to 1.2.0 (theirs) both land; gamma 2.0.0 in groups=['dev'] and delta 0.3 (adds from either side) land; legacy (deleted-one-side, untouched-other) is removed.
must_include: changed on both sides but identically
added on only one side is kept
deleted on one side and untouched on the other

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_clean_three_way_merge: alpha_files and beta_files each equal the set of two rows from the version that was kept (alpha-1.1.0 and beta-1.2.0 rows); dependencies=['beta>=1.0'] survives.

test_clean_three_way_merge: metadata.groups == ['default','dev'], strategy == ['inherit_metadata'], lock_version == '4.5.1', content_hash ends with '2'*64 (ours), targets == [{'requires_python': '>=3.9'}].
test_merge_output_is_a_wellformed_lockfile: file starts with `# This file is @generated by PDM.` header; test_merge_is_deterministic: byte-identical repeat runs; packages sorted by name.
must_include: load correctly through PDM's own lockfile reading logic

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_default_output_overwrites_ours: without -o, the merged result overwrites ours in place; package set becomes {alpha, beta, gamma, delta} with alpha 1.1.0 and beta 1.2.0.

test_version_conflict_fails_without_strategy: two sides bump alpha to different versions; return code != 0; stdout+stderr contains `alpha`, `1.1.0`, `1.5.0`; the -o target is not created; ours is byte-identical to before.
must_include: both sides bumping the same package to different versions

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_version_conflict_strategies: --on-conflict=newer picks 1.5.0 (higher); ours picks 1.1.0; theirs picks 1.5.0; newer includes the file row `alpha-1.5.0.tar.gz` in the file list.

test_removal_vs_modification_is_a_conflict: default fail returns non-zero with 'alpha' in message; --on-conflict=newer keeps alpha 1.1.0 (modification beats deletion); --on-conflict=theirs applies the deletion so alpha is absent.
must_include: one side deleting a package while the other modifies it

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_dry_run_writes_nothing: --dry-run on clean input returns 0 and writes no files; --dry-run on conflicting input returns non-zero and writes no files; ours is byte-identical throughout.
must_include: exits non-zero when there are conflicts

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_json_report: --json emits a JSON report on stdout with keys `clean`, `packages`, `changes.{added,removed,updated}`, `conflicts`; on clean, packages==4 and each of gamma/delta appears in added, legacy in removed, alpha and beta in updated; on conflict, rc!=0 with clean=false and 'alpha' in a conflict's `package` field; the -o target is not created.

test_diverging_lock_strategies_are_rejected: ours has static_urls-added strategy, theirs has cross_platform-added strategy; merge returns non-zero with 'strategy' present in output; no -o target is created.
test_strategy_change_on_one_side_is_merged: ours added static_urls; merged metadata.strategy contains 'static_urls' and alpha's files rows all have a 'url' key.
must_include: only one side changed them, take the changed side

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_invalid_inputs_are_rejected: --help works; missing file, pylock.toml as one of the inputs, and malformed TOML each return non-zero.
must_include: only the PDM format is supported

requirements.verifier_assertion: test_merged_lockfile_is_consumable_by_pdm: the merged file loads through `pdm.project.lockfile.pdmlock.PDMLock`; lock_version parses; version.major==spec.major and version.minor<=spec.minor; packages sorted; each package has a version; the check prints 'ok'.
must_include: load correctly through PDM's own lockfile reading logic
